title: Sarah Vaughan snaps at him at Union Station: 'Go on through the door'
summary: After an all-night stay at a Fourteenth Street after-hours spot, Malachi holds the station door for Sarah and is cursed out, later understanding she wants to be one of the guys.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: My first experience with that came the night of the second engagement that we had in Washington. Actually, it was the morning after the night we played the engagement. The next morning, we were to catch the train to go down to Rocky Mountain, North Carolina. I think the train was leaving at 8 o'clock or something. So we all stayed up that night in one of the after-hours spots on Fourteenth Street there, that was run by a guy that all the musicians knew. He had a piano in this place and everything. All the musicians used to go there and drink. So we decided to just stay up because of the early hour that we'd have to leave; stay up and just go from there to the train station.
I'd like to add that we rode the train then only because it was during the War, and gasoline was rationed. So all travel was by train. You couldn't have a bus then.
Anyway, it's Monday morning. We're in this place, and there was this girl that I'd just met at rehearsal, and a

couple of other musicians and I got a cab down to the Union Station in Washington. And as we got out of the cab and were paying the cab driver, each one of us had two bags -- we'd have maybe a large bag to carry your suits and whatever, and then you had a small bag with toiletries and other clothes and whatever. So we're getting out of the cab, we've all got two bags, and we get to the door of the station, which are swinging doors. So the doors are swinging -- and Sarah's walking along with me. When I got to the door, I opened the door and held it back for Sarah to come through, gentleman that I am -- or was. And I'm standing up there. And Sarah, this girl that I hardly know, I've just smiled and spoken to on the bandstand a couple of times and at rehearsal, looks at me and says, 'What are you standing up there looking at me for, fool? Go on through the door.' Somehow, it hurt me, because I had never... I thought she would be happy that I was holding the door. She said, 'You damn fool' or something like that. First of all, I don't know why this girl is talking to me like this, you know...

Anyway, I went on through the door and she came on in. But later on, after seeing how she was with the guys in the band, I understood and realized... And of course, we were friends, we've been friends ever since. But it was never an angry thing, but I was more hurt than ever, because I didn't

understand that kind of behavior, you know, coming from a girl. But I realized, after this... Her relationship to the guys in the band was just like she was one of them. You couldn't do anything for her. You talk about women's lib. She was liberated long before any woman that I know.
